_note: What each agent should DO. agents-config.json says how it runs (model, provider, enabled); this says what work it performs. Edit the instruction and the agent does something different on its next run -- no rebuild. context lists vault-relative files to include; paths are resolved and refused if they leave vault/. maxContextChars keeps a long log from blowing the prompt (and, for claude-agent, the bill); the TAIL of each file is kept, since these are append-only.

claude-agent.instruction: You are reviewing the ValhallaAI coordination log. Read the most recent entries and reply with exactly three sections, no preamble: (1) DONE -- the last three things that were actually completed, one line each. (2) OPEN -- anything explicitly flagged as unfinished, unverified, or needing a follow-up pass, one line each. (3) RISK -- the single item most likely to break next, and why, in one sentence. Do not invent items that are not in the log.

hermes-agent.instruction: You are auditing the ValhallaAI agent configuration. Compare the configured agents against the coordination log and reply with exactly two sections, no preamble: (1) CONFIG -- each agent, whether it is enabled, and the model it is set to use. (2) CONCERNS -- any agent whose configured model or credential looks stale or missing based on the log, one line each, or the single word NONE. Be brief.

grok-build.instruction: You are checking the ValhallaAI vault for drift. Read the coordination log and reply with exactly two sections, no preamble: (1) CLAIMS -- up to three statements the log makes about the current state of the project that a reader could verify against the code. (2) STALE -- any claim that a later entry appears to contradict, one line each, or the single word NONE.
